product_family: Durable execution / workflow orchestration platform used to build reliable applications and AI agents. Two distinct offerings: the open-source, self-hosted Temporal Server, and the managed Temporal Cloud SaaS.

privacy.ai_training_note: Temporal is a durable-execution/workflow-orchestration engine, not a generative AI model provider. The Data Processing Agreement states Temporal 'does not use customer workflow data for any purpose other than delivery of service,' and no vendor page mentions using customer data to train AI/ML models. Temporal's homepage markets the platform as infrastructure for OTHER companies' AI agents (OpenAI, Cursor, Replit, Retool build agent workflows on top of Temporal) -- Temporal itself does not process or train on the content of those agents' conversations beyond running the workflow.
privacy.data_region: Namespace-level regional isolation on AWS/GCP/Azure; docs state 'Namespaces do not share data processing or data storage across regional boundaries' but do not enumerate the specific region list.

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: TLS 1.3 for all connections to Temporal Cloud, regardless of authentication method

security.name: Encryption at rest
security.value: AES-256-GCM across Elasticsearch and the core persistence layer

security.name: Client-side / end-to-end encryption
security.value: Optional Data Converter encrypts payloads before they leave the customer's environment; optional Codec Server allows secure Web UI decryption without sharing keys with Temporal

security.name: Network isolation
security.value: Workers poll Temporal Cloud outbound only (no inbound connections into customer VPCs); AWS PrivateLink and GCP Private Service Connect supported

security.name: Tenant isolation
security.value: Namespace is the isolation boundary; per-Namespace mTLS or API key auth, plus separate Actions-Per-Second / Operations-Per-Second rate limits to prevent noisy-neighbor issues

security.name: Third-party audits
security.value: Annual third-party audit(s) and annual third-party penetration testing, per Trust Center quick-summary

security.name: Vulnerability disclosure
security.value: Has a bug bounty / vulnerability disclosure program; Temporal Technologies is a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) and publishes CVEs for the open-source server

security.name: Access management
security.value: Centralized IAM/SSO used to manage employee access, per Trust Center quick-summary

security.name: Subprocessors
security.value: Published subprocessor list (7 entries): Auth0, AWS, Elastic, Google Cloud, IBM, Microsoft Azure, WorkOS

products.name: Temporal Server (open source)
products.data_scope: All workflow state and data remain entirely within the customer's own infrastructure; Temporal Technologies has no access.
products.notes: Free and open source (MIT-licensed core); no vendor certifications apply because the customer operates and secures the deployment themselves.

products.name: Temporal Cloud
products.data_scope: Typical data access per Trust Center: username, email address, and business workflow state (event histories); payloads can be end-to-end encrypted client-side via the Data Converter so Temporal never sees plaintext.
products.notes: Holds SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA per the Trust Center; GDPR/CCPA compliance posture backed by a DPA and Standard Contractual Clauses. Namespace-level regional isolation across AWS/GCP/Azure.

compare.pricing_model: Temporal Cloud: usage-based (Actions Per Second and storage/retention); Temporal Server: free, open source, self-hosted (customer bears infrastructure cost).
compare.data_residency: Customer-selectable cloud region (AWS/GCP/Azure) for Temporal Cloud Namespaces; namespaces do not share data processing or storage across regional boundaries. Fully self-hosted option available for full data residency control.

flags: No ISO 27001 (or ISO 27017/27018/27701) certification found anywhere on the vendor's own domain -- graded held=false, not an oversight.

CCPA is listed as a Trust Center 'badge' alongside SOC 2/GDPR/HIPAA; it is a legal compliance posture rather than a third-party-audited certification, but is included here because the vendor itself presents it at the same tier.

Self-hosted Temporal Server and managed Temporal Cloud have materially different security postures -- certifications (SOC 2, HIPAA) apply only to Temporal Cloud, not to self-hosted deployments. Listing should make this product-level distinction explicit rather than applying certs directory-wide.
Data residency region list is not fully enumerated by the vendor in public docs (only isolation guarantees are documented).
